subject: general
question: Which water body separates Andaman in the north and Nicobar in the south?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ten Degree Channel.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Ten Degree Channel is a **narrow strip of water that runs between the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and is approximately 150 km wide.**
 
• The channel got its name as it lies on the **10th degree of north latitude.**
 
• The channel is an important shipping route as it connects the** Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eight Degree Channel: **

 
 
• The Eight Degree Channel is a significant waterway located in the Indian Ocean separates the islands of Minicoy (part of India's Lakshadweep archipelago) to the north and the Maldives to the south.
 
• This channel is significant for navigation, serving as a key sea route between the Arabian Sea and the central parts of the Indian Ocean.
 
 
 
• 
 
**Nine Degree Channel:**

 
 
• 
 
The Nine Degree Channel separates the Lakshadweep islands of Minicoy (Maliku Atoll) from the Lakshadweep group of islands to the north. It lies along the 9th parallel north of the equator.

 
 
• 
 
It is roughly 200 kilometers wide and is a crucial maritime route, offering passage between the Lakshadweep Sea (a part of the Arabian Sea) and the broader Indian Ocean.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
**Eleven Degree Channel:**

 
 
• 
 
The Eleven Degree Channel does not separate the Andaman and Nicobar Islands; instead, it lies between Little Andaman and Car Nicobar islands, marking the boundary between the Andaman Islands to the north and the Nicobar Islands to the south.

 
 
 

Hence, The correct answer is **option 1, Ten Degree Channel, **which separates Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
